The structure is described in the tetragonal body-centered space group I422 (space-group number 97, Hall symbol I 4 2), but the supplied input cell is not the conventional tetragonal cell. The input lattice is given by three equal edge lengths of 6.83406821 Å, with interaxial angles α = 104.12518159°, β = 104.12518159°, and γ = 120.79163825°, defining a rhombohedrally distorted seven-atom cell containing one Sr, two Ga, and four Te atoms. Fractional coordinates are used throughout, and the input fractional coordinates q_input are related to the conventional standard fractional coordinates q_standard by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the transformation matrix P has rows (0.5, −0.5, 0.5), (−0.5, 0.5, 0.5), and (−0.5, −0.5, 0.5), and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0), so no translational offset is applied between the two frames.

In the conventional I422 description, the independent atomic content reduces to three symmetry-inequivalent orbits. Strontium occupies Wyckoff site 2a at fractional position (0, 0, 0), with multiplicity two, so the two Sr atoms of the conventional cell are generated directly by the body-centering and tetragonal symmetry operations from the origin. Gallium occupies Wyckoff site 4c with representative coordinates (0, 1/2, 0), giving four equivalent Ga positions in the conventional cell. Tellurium occupies the eightfold Wyckoff site 8j, whose representative position is (x, x + 1/2, 1/4) with the single free parameter x = 0.3255215; thus the representative Te atom sits at approximately (0.3255215, 0.8255215, 0.25), and the remaining seven Te positions of the conventional cell follow from the I422 symmetry operations. Together these orbits account for the conventional-cell composition Sr₂Ga₄Te₈, while the original input cell, being smaller, contains SrGa₂Te₄.

The input coordinates were rounded to six decimal places before correction, and four small precision adjustments are required to recover the exact input geometry rather than an idealized symmetry-constrained approximation. A Te atom listed at input fractional position (0.075521, 0.575521, 0.151043) is displaced by (+0.000001, +0.000001, 0). A second Te atom at (0.424479, 0.924479, 0.848957) is displaced by (−0.000001, −0.000001, 0). A third Te atom at (0.924479, 0.075521, 0.5) is displaced by (−0.000001, +0.000001, 0). A fourth Te atom at (0.575521, 0.424479, 0.5) is displaced by (+0.000001, −0.000001, 0). These corrections are purely in-plane fractional shifts of order 10⁻⁶ and leave the z coordinates unchanged; they preserve the real input geometry while remaining consistent with the stated rounding precision.
